items.subject: Ollama 0.33.3 changed what prompt_eval_duration measures
items.what_happened: Ollama 0.33.3 changed the semantics of the prompt_eval_duration field so it no longer measures the same prefill interval as in prior releases. Operators comparing prefill/TTFT benchmarks or dashboards built on Ollama's API timing fields across versions will see discontinuous numbers and should re-baseline their metrics.

items.subject: LLMjacking: AI Model Hijacking Reaches Black Market Scale
items.what_happened: CSA research documents LLMjacking, where stolen credentials for LLM API endpoints are resold on black markets to run inference on someone else's infrastructure at their cost. Operators exposing self-hosted inference endpoints (vLLM, Ollama, TGI) should verify authentication is enforced, rotate leaked keys, and monitor for unexpected token consumption or unfamiliar client traffic.

classification.summary: OpenDocBot is a Show HN project that adds an AI assistant to Word, Excel and PowerPoint while letting users point it at their own model endpoint, including local backends such as Ollama or other OpenAI-compatible servers. platforms.name: llama.cpp
platforms.notes: Backend table has no Gaudi/Habana entry. Tensor-parallel split mode is explicitly EXPERIMENTAL and unimplemented for most MoE/hybrid architectures (expert placement instead relies on manual --n-cpu-moe/--override-tensor flags). FP8 is not a first-class ggml dtype — it exists only as the internal scale format inside MXFP4/NVFP4 blocks. AWQ/GPTQ GGUF-conversion tooling was removed/never supported.

platforms.name: LMDeploy
platforms.notes: AMD is partial: a ROCm install path exists (LMDEPLOY_TARGET_DEVICE=rocm) but KV-cache quantization docs restrict to CUDA/Ascend and the internal device_type validator omits rocm. No CPU-only backend (device_type validator allows only cuda/ascend/maca/camb). Speculative decoding (EAGLE/EAGLE3) is explicitly labeled experimental. Also supports Moore Threads MACA and Cambricon NPU (outside this matrix's hardware keys).

platforms.name: MLX-LM
platforms.notes: MLX is no longer Apple-only: mlx core now ships an official CUDA backend for Linux/NVIDIA (pip install mlx[cuda12]) and a separate CPU-only Linux backend, alongside its original Metal/Apple-Silicon path — mlx-lm's own setup.py confirms this at the package level (extras_require cuda12/cuda13/cpu each pull in the matching mlx[...] backend, overriding the base install_requires' Darwin-only mlx dependency) — no AMD/Gaudi/Ascend backend exists in either repo. GGUF is export-only and limited to Mistral/Mixtral/Llama-style models (mlx-lm cannot load a .gguf file for inference). KV-cache quantization is integer/affine, not FP8-format.

platforms.name: Ollama
platforms.notes: Judged on Ollama's own documented behavior, not inherited llama.cpp capability. gpu.mdx (the dedicated hardware doc) covers only Nvidia/AMD-ROCm/Metal/Vulkan — no Ascend or Gaudi section. No tensor-parallel/split-mode flag is exposed; MoE expert-offload PRs are unmerged. Speculative decoding merged only on the Apple-Silicon MLX runner for specific models — the general feature request is still open. No hybrid state-space models in Ollama's library (Jamba/Mamba/Falcon-Mamba all 404 on ollama.com). nvfp4 downgraded to partial: import.mdx's own quantize docs list only q8_0/q4_K_S/q4_K_M, and NVFP4-tagged models exist on ollama.com/library (e.g. qwen3.6:27b-coding-nvfp4) but loading one hits an open, unresolved crash — issue #16056 reports `ggml.c:1676: GGML_ASSERT(type >= 0 && type < GGML_TYPE_COUNT) failed` loading an NVFP4 GGUF; the corresponding llama.cpp PR is linked but not yet ported to Ollama's fork.

platforms.name: SGLang
platforms.notes: intel_gaudi marked partial: no dedicated hardware-platform guide (overview.mdx lists only nvidia/amd/ascend/cpu/jetson/tpu/xpu), but --device accepts "hpu" and a legacy HpuCommunicator class exists (inherited from the vLLM lineage). gguf is NVIDIA+Ascend only — no AMD/ROCm (Marlin-kernel dependent).

platforms.name: TensorRT-LLM
platforms.notes: NVIDIA-only, proprietary TensorRT compiler stack — no AMD/Gaudi/ Apple/Ascend/CPU inference path in any fetched doc. Disaggregated serving is documented as mature but limited to decoder-only models at beam width 1. GGUF is never mentioned (TRT-LLM uses its own ModelOpt checkpoint/engine format).

platforms.name: Text Generation Inference (TGI)
platforms.notes: TGI is in maintenance mode as of this verification (README: only bug-fix/doc PRs accepted, recommends vLLM/SGLang/llama.cpp/MLX going forward). ep_size != 1 explicitly raises for DeepSeek-V2 (expert parallel unsupported); no pipeline-parallel or hybrid Mamba/Jamba model support found. AMD/ROCm does not support AWQ checkpoint loading.

platforms.name: vLLM
platforms.notes: Apple GPU support ships via the vllm-project-org vllm-metal plugin (MLX backend); Gaudi/Ascend likewise via official out-of-tree vllm-project plugins, not the in-tree core. GGUF requires the separate vllm-gguf-plugin. Disaggregated prefill is documented but the page itself is titled "experimental".

alerts.subject: Shodan indexes over 47.000 exposed Ollama instances
alerts.what_happened: A Shodan scan reportedly indexes over 47,000 Ollama instances reachable on the public internet, which by default expose unauthenticated API endpoints allowing model listing, pulling, deletion, and inference. Operators should verify OLLAMA_HOST binding, keep port 11434 off public interfaces, and place any external access behind an authenticating reverse proxy or VPN. Note: the source is a single social media post, so the figure is unverified.

alerts.subject: Ollama 0.33.3 changed what prompt_eval_duration measures
alerts.what_happened: Ollama 0.33.3 changed the semantics of the prompt_eval_duration field so it no longer measures the same prefill interval as in prior releases. Operators comparing prefill/TTFT benchmarks or dashboards built on Ollama's API timing fields across versions will see discontinuous numbers and should re-baseline their metrics.

alerts.subject: Scaling Multi-GPU Video Captioning with PyNvVideoCodec and vLLM
alerts.what_happened: vLLM blog describes using NVIDIA's PyNvVideoCodec library to offload video decoding to GPU hardware decoders in multi-GPU video captioning pipelines with vision-language models. Operators running self-hosted VLM inference on NVIDIA GPUs can use this pattern to remove CPU-side decode bottlenecks and improve throughput scaling.

alerts.subject: Show HN: Swift-Qwen3.8-27B, -58.3% thinking, x1.95 speed, accuracy of xhigh
alerts.what_happened: A community-published derivative of Qwen3 (27B), Swift-Qwen3.8-27B, is available as open weights on Hugging Face, claiming 58.3% fewer thinking tokens and ~1.95x throughput while matching high-reasoning-effort accuracy. Operators running reasoning models on self-hosted vLLM stacks could evaluate it for reduced decode cost, though the performance claims are vendor-supplied and unverified.

alerts.subject: vLLM x Novita AI: Chord, Faster INT4 MoE for Kimi K2.x. Up to 1.3x on H200, 2.15x on Untuned B300
alerts.what_happened: Novita AI open-sourced Chord, a W4A16 INT4 MoE CUDA kernel targeting Kimi K2.x serving shapes in vLLM, with a Humming-compatible indexed path and grouped SM90 operators. Reported speedups are up to 1.3x on H200 and 2.15x on untuned B300, so operators serving quantized Kimi K2.x on Hopper/Blackwell GPUs may gain throughput by adopting it.

alerts.subject: Kimi K3 Performance Optimizations in vLLM: The Road to 2.8× Throughput
alerts.what_happened: vLLM documents serving optimizations for Kimi K3 claiming up to 2.8x throughput, covering scheduling, KDA prefix caching, ReplaySSM state recovery, prefill-decode disaggregation with state offload, parallelism strategies, MoE handling, and GPU kernels. Operators serving Kimi K3 on vLLM can adopt these settings on a recent vLLM build for higher throughput; no action required otherwise.

alerts.subject: LLM 0.35
alerts.what_happened: Simon Willison released version 0.35 of the LLM CLI tool, which supports querying local models via plugins (e.g. llama.cpp, Ollama, and OpenAI-compatible endpoints such as vLLM). Operators using LLM for scripted access to self-hosted models can upgrade for the new features and fixes in this release.

alerts.subject: Glq a port trellis quantization of large language models as a vLLM plugin
alerts.what_happened: GLQ is an open-source vLLM plugin implementing port trellis quantization for large language models, allowing self-hosted operators to serve models with an alternative low-bit quantization scheme. As a third-party plugin it is early-stage and would need validation against existing vLLM quantization paths before production use.

alerts.subject: Tiered KV Cache Offloading in vLLM
alerts.what_happened: vLLM describes a host-centric tiered KV cache offloading framework that extends cache storage beyond GPU memory into host RAM, local filesystems, object stores, and remote peers. Operators can use it to cut prefix recomputation and serve more concurrent requests on the same GPU footprint.

alerts.subject: Following the Bottleneck: Optimizing MiniMax M3 on AMD Instinct MI355X
alerts.what_happened: vLLM documents a step-by-step performance-tuning methodology applied to serving MiniMax M3 on AMD Instinct MI355X, covering kernel shape inspection, elimination of redundant work, data-movement and dispatch verification, and queue analysis. Operators running vLLM on ROCm/MI355X hardware can reuse the described optimizations and profiling approach to raise throughput.

alerts.subject: vLLM 0.29.0: Model Runner V2 is now the default
alerts.what_happened: vLLM 0.29.0 makes Model Runner V2 the default execution path for model loading and inference scheduling. Operators upgrading should validate throughput, memory footprint, and custom model/plugin compatibility against the new runner, and can fall back to the legacy runner if regressions appear.

alerts.subject: GLM 5.3 Optimizations, Part 1: Hybrid HiSparse Offloading in vLLM
alerts.what_happened: vLLM adds HiSparse as a pressure-driven memory tier that works alongside the Hybrid Memory Allocator and KV offloading, so GLM 5.3 requests can continue decoding when their KV cache exceeds GPU memory. Operators serving GLM 5.3 can sustain higher concurrency without hitting hard KV capacity limits.

alerts.subject: vLLM x AgentX: Optimizing for Real-World Agentic Serving
alerts.what_happened: vLLM describes optimizations for agentic serving workloads, covering KV cache management, parallelism strategies, scheduling, and prefill/decode disaggregation, benchmarked on the SemiAnalysis AgentX suite at up to 130K tokens per GPU-second. Operators running agentic workloads on vLLM can use these configuration and feature notes to tune throughput and cost per token on self-hosted GPUs.

alerts.subject: Serving LLMs on Tenstorrent Hardware: Inside the vLLM TT Plugin
alerts.what_happened: vLLM gains Tenstorrent accelerator support via an out-of-tree platform plugin, adding phase-based scheduling, single-process data parallelism on Galaxy systems, on-device sampling with host fallback, and async decode overlap. Operators evaluating non-NVIDIA inference hardware can now serve models on Tenstorrent devices through the standard vLLM interface.

alerts.subject: GLM 5.3 Optimizations, Part 1: Hybrid HiSparse Offloading in vLLM
alerts.what_happened: vLLM adds HiSparse as a pressure-driven memory tier that works with the Hybrid Memory Allocator and KV offloading, so GLM 5.3 requests continue decoding when their KV cache exceeds GPU memory. Operators serving GLM 5.3 can sustain higher concurrency without hard OOM-driven preemption.
